import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    correlated_pairs = set()
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    X = feats.x
    n_features = X.shape[1]
    
    # Calculate correlations
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(X.T)
    
    # Identify near-duplicates
    for i in range(n_features):
        for j in range(i+1, n_features):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= corr_threshold:
                correlated_pairs.add((feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]))
    
    # Select features to consider (remove one from each near-duplicate pair)
    selected_ids = []
    used_ids = set()
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if fid in used_ids:
            continue
            
        # Check if this feature is part of any correlated pair
        is_correlated = False
        for pair in correlated_pairs:
            if fid in pair:
                other_fid = pair[0] if pair[0] != fid else pair[1]
                # Keep the one with higher t-statistic
                used_ids.add(other_fid)
                is_correlated = True
                break
        
        if not is_correlated:
            selected_ids.append(fid)
    
    # Calculate t-statistics for all selected features
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if fid in selected_ids:
            x1 = X[feats.y == 1, i]
            x0 = X[feats.y == 0, i]
            if len(x1) > 0 and len(x0) > 0:
                t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(x1, x0, equal_var=False)
                t_stats.append((abs(t_stat), fid))
            else:
                t_stats.append((0, fid))
    
    # Sort by absolute t-statistic
    t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top features for drivers (at most MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = [fid for _, fid in t_stats[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # For columns, include all selected features
    columns = tuple(selected_ids)
    
    # For products, look for strong pairwise interactions among top features
    products = []
    top_fids = [fid for _, fid in t_stats[:min(10, len(t_stats))]]
    
    # Simple approach: add products of top features if they're not too correlated
    for i, a in enumerate(top_fids):
        for b in top_fids[i+1:]:
            # Check if already in correlation matrix with high correlation
            idx_a = feats.column(a)
            idx_b = feats.column(b)
            if idx_a < X.shape[1] and idx_b < X.shape[1]:
                corr = abs(np.corrcoef(X[:, idx_a], X[:, idx_b])[0,1])
                if corr < 0.7:  # Avoid adding highly correlated products
                    products.append((a, b))
    
    # Loadings: assign weights based on t-statistic magnitude
    loadings = {}
    for abs_t, fid in t_stats:
        if abs_t > 0:
            loadings[fid] = abs_t
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
